For an integration task (position is the time-ordered double integral of acceleration), order is the entire signal. Also d_model = X.shape[-1] (the raw feature width, ~9-10) with nhead=1 and TransformerEncoderLayer defaulting to batch_first=False while the data is fed batch-first (X_batch is (batch, seq, feat)), so the layer treats the batch dimension as the sequence/time dimension and the time dimension as batch — attention mixes across the wrong axis.
bugs.why_wrong: A transformer over a temporal IMU window must inject positional information and must agree on the (seq,batch,feat) vs (batch,seq,feat) layout. Here neither holds: no positional encoding, and batch_first is left at its False default while batch-first tensors are passed, silently swapping time and batch.
bugs.fix_sketch: Add sinusoidal/learned positional encoding sized to d_model and seq_len; project raw features to a sensible d_model (e.g. 32-64) via a linear input embedding so d_model is divisible by nhead and not tied to 9; pass batch_first=True to TransformerEncoderLayer (or transpose to (seq,batch,feat)). Then choose an explicit sequence reduction (last token / mean pool / CLS) before the position head.

bugs.title: Train loss uses only the last timestep while validation loss uses the whole sequence (mismatched objective)
bugs.lines: cell 4 (training: loss = criterion(outputs[:,-1:,:], y_batch[:,-1:,:]); validation: loss = criterion(outputs, y_batch))
bugs.description: In the training loop the loss is computed on outputs[:,-1:,:] vs y_batch[:,-1:,:] (only the final timestep), but the validation loop computes criterion(outputs, y_batch) over the FULL sequence. The model is therefore optimized for one objective and selected/early-stopped on a different one. EarlyStopping (patience 30) and checkpointing key off this incomparable val loss. Because there is no positional encoding and time/batch axes are swapped (bug above), 'last timestep' is not even a well-defined temporal endpoint.
bugs.why_wrong: Train and validation losses must measure the same quantity for the val curve and early stopping to be meaningful. Optimizing the last-token MSE but monitoring full-sequence MSE makes model selection arbitrary.
bugs.fix_sketch: Make train and val losses identical — either supervise the full per-timestep sequence in both, or reduce to a single predicted position (e.g. last token after a proper reduction) in both.

bugs.title: position_estimate calls load_split_data with stale kwargs -> silently loads 1000 samples and then crashes on unpacking
bugs.description: load_split_data (utils.py 230-392) expects N_train/N_test and returns FIVE values (X_train,y_train,X_test,y_test,col_locations). This notebook passes Ntrain/Nval (not recognized — params.update just adds dead keys, so N_train stays the default 1000 and N_test stays 100; I verified the 1,000,000 is ignored) and unpacks only two: X, y = load_split_data(...). That is a ValueError (too many values to unpack). It also references torch/nn/F/TensorDataset/DataLoader that are never imported in this notebook (cell 0 only does from utils import *). So this notebook cannot run as written, and even if patched it would train on 1000 samples, not the intended million. calculate_position_difference(y) (utils.py 401-404) then mutates y in place subtracting the window's first position — fine as a relative-target choice, but combined with split_data being purely temporal it is the only thing preventing leakage here.
bugs.why_wrong: The data-loading contract (arg names + 5-tuple return) changed but this caller was never updated, so the experiment silently runs on 1000 points (or crashes). Results from this notebook are not what the config claims.
bugs.fix_sketch: Use the current API: X_train,y_train,X_test,y_test,col_locations = load_split_data(folder_path, N_train=..., N_test=..., seq_len=..., input=..., output=...). Import torch and friends. Confirm the loaded sample count matches intent.

bugs.title: Quaternion normalization in transformer forward() reduces over the wrong axis / by a scalar
bugs.lines: cell 4 forward(): 'quats = quats / torch.norm(quats)' ; transformer_2_anton.ipynb cell 0 forward(): 'quats = quats / torch.norm(quats, dim=1)'
bugs.description: After the quat_cleaner produces a (1, seq, 4) tensor, transformer_initial normalizes with torch.norm(quats) which is the Frobenius norm of the ENTIRE tensor (a single scalar over all timesteps and components), not a per-quaternion unit normalization. transformer_2 uses dim=1 (the sequence axis) instead of the component axis (dim=-1), so it divides each component by the norm taken across time. Neither yields unit quaternions per timestep. Per-quaternion normalization must be over the 4-component axis (dim=-1, keepdim=True). The earlier per-step normalization next_quat/torch.norm(next_quat) inside the loop is correct for a single 4-vector, but the batched cleaner output is not.
bugs.why_wrong: A rotation quaternion must have unit norm per timestep; normalizing by a tensor-wide scalar or along the time axis leaves non-unit quaternions, so quat_2_rotation_matrix / downstream rotation are no longer valid rotations.
bugs.fix_sketch: quats = quats / torch.norm(quats, dim=-1, keepdim=True). Apply the same per-quaternion normalization everywhere a quaternion is produced.

bugs.title: Hand-rolled physics-informed integration uses wrong physics (gravity not removed, bogus p formula) feeding the transformer
bugs.lines: preprocess_data: v=cumsum(acc)*1/200 ; p=cumsum(v)*1/200 + cumsum(acc**2)*1/200**2/2 ; acc only mean-zeroed per window
bugs.description: Although not in the explicit notebook list, this is the operationalized version of the integration the assignment targets, and it inherits the same bugs plus new ones. It only subtracts each window's first acce value (X[:, :1, acc] — removing the initial sample, not gravity), rotates by orientations derived from the inverted get_body2world_rot, then computes position as p = cumsum(v)*dt + cumsum(acc**2)*dt^2/2. The second term integrates the SQUARE of acceleration (cumsum of a**2), which is dimensionally and physically meaningless — the kinematic term should be 0.5*a*dt^2, i.e. 0.5*cumsum(a)*dt^2, not cumsum(a**2). Squaring also destroys sign. So the 'calced/position' feature handed to the network is physically wrong.
bugs.why_wrong: Trapezoidal/Euler double integration is p += v*dt + 0.5*a*dt^2 with a the (gravity-removed, world-frame) acceleration; there is no a^2 anywhere. Subtracting only the first sample is not gravity removal.
bugs.fix_sketch: Remove gravity in world frame (use linacce or subtract g_world after a correct R), then p = cumsum(cumsum(a)*dt)*dt (or proper trapezoidal). Drop the cumsum(a**2) term entirely.

bugs.title: Overlapping windows + random train/test split create train/test leakage in the integration pipeline
bugs.lines: load_split_data overlap=1 then train_test_split(..., random_state=42) over windows; also Acce_Ori_to_Pos.ipynb
bugs.description: create_sequences (utils.py 82-105) with overlap=1 produces windows whose stride = seq_len-1, so adjacent windows share samples; transformer_informed then does a RANDOM train_test_split over these windows, so near-duplicate windows land in both train and val, leaking. Acce_Ori_to_Pos.ipynb is worse: it concatenates train and test back together (Xtotal/ytotal cells 32-34) and then re-runs train_test_split on the original X,y (cells 38-41) with overlapping context, and StandardScaler is fit then the result discarded (ct.transform return value never assigned, cells 12/39), so scaling is a no-op too. utils.load_split_data also has a related leakage smell: in the multi-dir case it vstacks new_data_dict[key][:N] (always from index 0) ignoring the random start, so train dirs after the first reuse the same leading samples.
bugs.why_wrong: For a temporal/integration task, splits must be by contiguous time segment (or by recording), never random over overlapping windows, or the val/test error is optimistic. Fitting a scaler and dropping the transformed output means no normalization is applied despite normalize=True intent.
bugs.fix_sketch: Split by recording/time block before windowing; if overlapping windows are needed, ensure no window crosses the split boundary. Assign the scaler output (X = ct.transform(X)) and fit only on train.

bugs.title: Per-window relative position target makes the absolute trajectory non-reconstructable / metric meaningless
bugs.lines: 401-404 (calculate_position_difference) and transformer_informed preprocess y -= y[:, :1, :]; y = y[:,-1,:]
bugs.description: calculate_position_difference subtracts each window's first position from the whole window, and transformer_informed sets y to the last sample of the per-window-zeroed position (y[:,-1,:]). Each window is thus zeroed independently, so the targets are per-window displacements with no shared origin. The test-time reconstruction then does np.cumsum over windows (transformer_informed) or the no-op batch loop (notebooks) to rebuild a trajectory — but cumsum of last-sample displacements of overlapping, independently-zeroed windows does not reconstruct the true absolute trajectory (the within-window start offset is lost, and overlap double counts). The MSE the model minimizes is therefore on a quantity that doesn't cleanly map back to trajectory error (e.g. ATE/RTE used by RoNIN).
bugs.why_wrong: To reconstruct an absolute trajectory you need consistent per-step displacements (velocity*dt) chained from a single origin, or absolute positions in a common frame. Independently zeroing each window and then cumsumming endpoint positions mixes frames and loses the inter-window offset.
bugs.fix_sketch: Predict per-step (or per-window) displacement in a consistent world frame, then integrate once from a single known origin; evaluate with a trajectory metric (ATE/RTE) rather than raw windowed MSE.

bugs.title: scheduler.step_size=0.1 (float) on StepLR is invalid/ineffective and scheduler steps per-batch
bugs.lines: cell 0 (StepLR(optim_, step_size=0.1, gamma=0.05); scheduler.step() inside batch loop); same in transformer_initial_anton.ipynb cell 4
bugs.description: StepLR expects an integer step_size (epochs). step_size=0.1 with scheduler.step() called every batch means the comparison last_epoch % step_size is ill-defined for a float and effectively decays the LR by gamma=0.05 almost immediately, collapsing the learning rate to ~0 within the first batches. Combined with batch_size=1 this means the model stops learning after a handful of samples.
bugs.why_wrong: StepLR.step_size must be a positive integer number of scheduler.step() calls; calling step() every batch with such a tiny effective period and aggressive gamma kills the LR before training meaningfully starts.
bugs.fix_sketch: Use an integer step_size in epochs (e.g. 10) and call scheduler.step() once per epoch, not per batch; or use a scheduler intended for per-batch stepping (OneCycleLR/cosine) with sane params.

research.topic: RoNIN — Robust Neural Inertial Navigation in the Wild (Herath, Yan, Furukawa; arXiv:1905.12853; ICRA 2020). Pedestrian inertial odometry from smartphone 6-DoF IMU (accel+gyro), regressing 2D motion in a heading-agnostic, gravity-aligned frame.
key_techniques: COORDINATE FRAME (Heading-Agnostic Coordinate Frame, HACF): The network does NOT work in the device frame or the global/world frame. It works in any frame whose Z axis is aligned with gravity (a 'heading-agnostic coordinate frame'). The yaw/heading is left arbitrary — there are infinitely many valid HACFs differing by a horizontal rotation. The raw IMU samples (accel + gyro, each a 3-vector) are rotated from the device frame into the HACF using the device orientation supplied by the platform's sensor-fusion attitude (Android Game Rotation Vector at training time; Android/iOS system device orientation at test time). The Game Rotation Vector is used (not the full Rotation Vector) so the estimate is magnetometer-independent — heading-agnostic. This sidesteps RIDI's stabilized-IMU singularity (which breaks when the Y axis points at gravity).

INPUT FEATURE: a window of 200 frames x 6 channels = a 200x6 tensor: the gravity-aligned accelerometer (3) and gyroscope (3) concatenated. Magnetometer is NOT fed to the position network (heading-agnostic). Both IMU and ground-truth pose are recorded at 200 Hz; processing/windowing is at 200 Hz.

OUTPUT TARGET: a 2D vector in the horizontal plane of the HACF. Because the frame is gravity-aligned and heading-free, the regressed motion is rotation-equivariant only up to the unknown horizontal heading — RoNIN learns motion relative to gravity and uses the system attitude to place it. The vertical (Z) component is discarded in evaluation; trajectories are evaluated in 2D.

THREE ARCHITECTURES — (1) RoNIN ResNet: a 1D version of standard ResNet-18 over the 200x6 input, with a final fully-connected layer (512 units) regressing a single 2D vector = the displacement (P_i - P_{i-200}) over the 200-frame (1 s) window. Output channels = 2 (vx, vy) [code expands to 3 for vz on some datasets but Z is dropped]. This is the headline/best model.

THREE ARCHITECTURES — (2) RoNIN LSTM: a stacked unidirectional LSTM, 3 layers x 100 hidden units, with a bilinear-layer input enrichment, emitting a per-frame 2D velocity. A non-trainable integration layer sums these per-frame velocities over a window to form a displacement that is supervised — the 'latent velocity loss'.

THREE ARCHITECTURES — (3) RoNIN TCN: a temporal convolutional network of 6 residual blocks with channel widths 16, 32, 64, 128, 72, 36, dilated conv kernels of size 3, giving a receptive field of 253 frames. Like the LSTM it emits per-frame 2D velocities passed through the integration layer.

LOSS — ResNet: plain MSE (torch.nn.MSELoss) between the network's 2D output at frame i and the ground-truth strided displacement P_i - P_{i-200} (a 'strided velocity'). LSTM/TCN: 'latent velocity loss' — the network outputs per-frame 2D velocities in a latent layer, an integration layer sums them over the window (~400 frames for LSTM, 253 for TCN), and the L2 norm is taken against the ground-truth positional difference over that same window. This integration-then-supervise design raises SNR of a noisy per-frame target.

TRAJECTORY RECONSTRUCTION: predicted 2D velocities/displacements are integrated by cumulative sum scaled by the timestep: pos[1:-1] = np.cumsum(preds[:, :2] * dts, axis=0) + pos[0]. There is no learned global heading in the position net — the platform attitude (heading) orients the per-window motion into a consistent frame. A separate ronin_body_heading.py network estimates body heading if a fully global trajectory is needed.

ATE (Absolute Trajectory Error): RMSE between the whole estimated and ground-truth 2D trajectories. Code: np.sqrt(np.mean((est - gt) ** 2)) over all matched timesteps (no SE(2)/Sim(3) alignment is applied in RoNIN's metric.py — it is a direct positional RMSE).

RTE (Relative Trajectory Error): mean over a sliding fixed-time window (default 1 minute = pred_per_min = 12000 frames at 200 Hz) of the RMSE of the relative endpoint drift. For a window delta, err = (est[delta:] - est[:-delta]) - (gt[delta:] - gt[:-delta]); rte = sqrt(mean(err**2)). For sequences shorter than 1 minute, it uses delta = N-1 (the whole sequence) and scales the result by pred_per_min / N to normalize to a 1-minute-equivalent drift.
concrete_recommendations: Regress motion in a gravity-aligned, heading-agnostic frame, NOT global position and NOT the device frame. Pipeline per window: (a) get per-sample device attitude from the platform's game rotation vector (gravity-aligned, magnetometer-free); (b) rotate accel and gyro 3-vectors into that HACF; (c) feed the 200x6 gravity-aligned IMU window to the net; (d) regress a 2D horizontal motion vector; (e) integrate by cumsum into a trajectory.

For the primary model, reimplement ResNet-18 as a 1D CNN (conv1d, batchnorm, residual blocks) over a 200x6 input, with a 512-unit FC head -> 2 outputs. Train with plain MSE against the 200-frame strided displacement target P_i - P_{i-200}. This is the simplest and strongest RoNIN variant — build it first.

Use window_size = 200 samples (1 s at 200 Hz) and training step_size = 10 (extract a sample every 10 frames). At test time you can predict more densely (e.g. every 5 frames) and integrate. Keep the 200 Hz pipeline; if your IMU is a different rate, resample to a fixed rate and recompute the per-window sample count so 1 window ~= 1 s.

Implement the LSTM (3x100 unidirectional + bilinear input layer) and TCN (6 residual blocks, channels 16/32/64/128/72/36, kernel 3, dilations giving RF=253) with a NON-trainable integration layer: net emits per-frame 2D velocity, sum over the window, then L2 vs the ground-truth window displacement (latent velocity loss). Don't supervise per-frame velocity directly — that is the SNR insight.

Apply random-yaw data augmentation: at each training step, rotate the ground-truth trajectory (and equivalently the HACF) by a random horizontal angle so the net becomes invariant to the arbitrary heading of the HACF. This is essential to make heading-agnostic training work.

Drop the vertical (Z) channel for trajectory evaluation; evaluate in 2D. Report ATE and RTE exactly as RoNIN: ATE = sqrt(mean((est-gt)^2)) over the whole trajectory; RTE = mean over a 1-minute (12000-frame @200Hz) sliding window of the relative-displacement-error RMSE, with the short-sequence scaling (delta=N-1, multiply by 12000/N). Reuse the metric.py logic verbatim to stay comparable.

Use the platform sensor-fusion attitude as an INPUT (to define the frame), not something you regress in the position net. Keep body-heading estimation as a separate model (RoNIN's ronin_body_heading.py) if you need a globally-oriented trajectory rather than a heading-agnostic one.

Match RoNIN's data conventions: timestamps -> per-sample dt; integrate with cumsum(preds[:, :2] * dts) + pos0; resample IMU to a uniform grid before windowing; align ground truth (the public dataset has Tango/3D-pose ground truth at 200 Hz).

pitfalls: Confusing the output frame: RoNIN does NOT regress global position or device-frame velocity. It regresses 2D motion in a gravity-aligned, heading-AGNOSTIC frame. Forgetting that the heading is arbitrary (and thus needing yaw augmentation) will make a naive reimplementation fail to generalize.

Feeding raw device-frame IMU: you must rotate accel+gyro into the gravity-aligned frame using the platform attitude (game rotation vector) BEFORE the network. Skipping this removes the whole inductive bias.

Using the magnetometer in the position network: RoNIN deliberately uses the magnetometer-free game rotation vector so the system is heading-agnostic and robust to magnetic disturbance. Including the magnetometer for the frame defeats this.
Supervising per-frame velocity directly for LSTM/TCN: the design is integrate-THEN-supervise (latent velocity loss over the window). Supervising raw per-frame velocities lowers SNR and underperforms.

Misimplementing RTE: it is NOT the full-trajectory error and NOT a per-frame error — it is the RMSE of RELATIVE displacement error over a fixed 1-minute (12000-frame @200Hz) sliding window, with a specific scaling for sequences shorter than a minute (delta=N-1, multiply by 12000/N). Getting the window or scaling wrong makes numbers incomparable to the paper.

Assuming ATE uses trajectory alignment: RoNIN's metric.py ATE is a direct positional RMSE with NO SE(2)/Sim(3) Umeyama alignment (unlike SLAM-style ATE). Reusing a SLAM ATE that pre-aligns trajectories will report different (usually lower) numbers.
Rate mismatch: everything (window=200, pred_per_min=12000, RF=253) is tied to 200 Hz. A different sensor rate requires recomputing all sample counts so a window stays ~1 s and RTE stays ~1 minute.
Forgetting to discard Z: RoNIN evaluates 2D; the vertical component is dropped. Comparing a 3D error against RoNIN's 2D ATE/RTE is apples-to-oranges.

Train vs test stride: training extracts a sample every step_size=10 frames; test predicts more densely (every ~5 frames). Using the training stride at inference under-samples the trajectory integration.

research.topic: IONet (AAAI 2018) and L-IONet: polar-vector regression for pedestrian inertial odometry from smartphone IMU
key_techniques: Polar-vector regression target: instead of regressing global position, the network maps a window of raw 6-channel IMU data to a 2D polar vector (Delta-l, Delta-psi) = (scalar displacement magnitude, heading CHANGE) over that window. Output dim is just 2.

Orientation-independent displacement derivation: starting from strapdown kinematics over a window, displacement Delta-L = C_b^n(0) * (n*v_b(0)*dt + T*dt^2 - (n(n-1)/2)*g_b0*dt^2), where v_b(0)=initial velocity in body frame, g_b0=gravity in body frame, T is the double-integrated acceleration term, n=window length. Taking the L2 norm Delta-l=||Delta-L||_2 kills the initial absolute orientation because the rotation matrix C_b^n(0) is orthogonal (C^T C = I preserves vector norm). So the displacement MAGNITUDE depends only on inertial data + initial velocity + gravity in the body frame, NOT on absolute heading. This is the core trick that makes the regression target observable from a single window.

Functional form learned by the net: (Delta-l, Delta-psi) = f_theta(v_b(0), g_b0, a_{1:n}, w_{1:n}); the net implicitly infers the unobservable latent states (initial velocity, gravity direction) from the raw window rather than requiring them as propagated state.

Windowing as 'integrator reset': inertial stream is sliced into independent windows; latent states are NOT propagated between windows. The authors explicitly liken this to resetting an integrator to prevent wind-up in classical control. This breaks the open-loop triple-integration chain that causes unbounded drift.

Window config: 200 frames = 2.0 s at 100 Hz IMU; sliding stride of 10 frames (0.1 s), giving a 10 Hz output rate. Window sizes 50/100/200/400 were tried; 200 chosen as best trade-off between accumulated location error and per-window prediction loss.

Architecture (IONet): 2-layer BIDIRECTIONAL LSTM, 96 hidden units per layer, 25% dropout during training, followed by a fully-connected regression layer FC(h_n) producing the 2-vector. Input is (a,w) of shape 200x6 (3 accel + 3 gyro). Magnetometer is NOT used by the core regressor.

Trajectory reconstruction (Cartesian composition): global heading accumulates psi_n = psi_{n-1} + Delta-psi, and position updates as L_n^x = L_0^x + Delta-l*cos(psi_0 + Delta-psi), L_n^y = L_0^y + Delta-l*sin(psi_0 + Delta-psi). So the net stays in a relative/per-window frame; absolute placement is done by trigonometric composition outside the network.

Loss: weighted sum of squared errors on the two outputs, ell = sum ||Delta-l_hat - Delta-l||^2 + kappa * ||Delta-psi_hat - Delta-psi||^2 (kappa balances displacement vs heading); trained with Adam, lr=1e-5, batch size 256, minimizing MSE between predicted and ground-truth polar vectors.

L-IONet (IEEE IoT Journal 2020) swaps the Bi-LSTM for a WaveNet-style feed-forward CNN: dilated CAUSAL convolutions with 8 layers, dilation 1,2,4,8,16,32,64,128 (receptive field ~ the 200-frame window), gated activation tanh(Wf*x) (elementwise) sigmoid(Wg*x), plus residual + skip connections, final FC(Pool(z)) -> same (Delta-l, Delta-psi) target. Same polar formulation, just a cheaper sequence model.

OxIOD dataset (introduced alongside L-IONet): 158 sequences, >42 km, 14.72 h; 100 Hz 6-axis IMU (+3-axis magnetometer present in raw data); devices iPhone 7 Plus / 6 / 5 and Nexus 5; attachments handheld / pocket / handbag / trolley; motion modes halting/slow/normal/running; Vicon mocap ground truth (sub-mm) plus Google Tango as pseudo-ground-truth for large-scale trials.
concrete_recommendations: Make the network output a 2D polar vector (Delta-l, Delta-psi) per window, NOT a global (x,y). Delta-l = displacement magnitude over the window; Delta-psi = heading CHANGE over the window. Reconstruct the trajectory outside the net by accumulating heading and applying x += Delta-l*cos(psi), y += Delta-l*sin(psi). This keeps the regression target observable and shift/rotation-invariant.

Use a fixed window of 200 samples (2.0 s) at 100 Hz with a sliding stride of 10 samples (10 Hz output). For a 200 Hz input stream, either downsample to 100 Hz to match the original setup or use ~400 samples per 2 s window and re-tune; keep window length around 1.5-2.5 s. Treat each window as INDEPENDENT — do not carry hidden state across windows (the 'integrator reset' that prevents drift wind-up).

Input tensor = window x 6 channels (3 accel + 3 gyro), normalized to a common scale per channel. The original core model omits the magnetometer; if you have it at 200 Hz you can add 3 mag channels as an ablation, but the published method works without it.

For the architecture, either reproduce the 2-layer bidirectional LSTM (96 hidden units/layer, 25% dropout, FC->2) for the IONet baseline, or implement the L-IONet WaveNet (8 dilated causal conv layers, dilations 1..128, gated tanh*sigmoid activations, residual+skip, global pool -> FC->2) for a ~4x smaller, ~10x faster-to-train, on-device-friendly model. Bidirectional is fine offline; for streaming/causal inference prefer the L-IONet causal-conv variant.

Loss = MSE on Delta-l plus weighted MSE on Delta-psi (tune kappa so the two terms are comparable in magnitude, since meters vs radians differ in scale). Train with Adam, lr~1e-5, batch 256 as a starting point.

Generate ground-truth polar labels from your mocap/VIO reference: for each window compute Delta-l = Euclidean distance between window endpoints in the horizontal plane, and Delta-psi = signed change in 2D heading (atan2 of the displacement direction, or integrated yaw) between consecutive windows. Wrap heading to (-pi, pi].

Post-process with low-pass filtering on the predicted polar vectors and on the reconstructed positions to suppress per-window jitter (used in the L-IONet pipeline). Update current position relative to the position one full window (200 frames) earlier rather than the position 10 frames earlier to match the sliding-window reconstruction.

Evaluate with cumulative position-error CDF (e.g., max error within 90% of test time) and against VIO/Tango pseudo-ground-truth on long trajectories; report position error at fixed distances (50 m, 100 m, endpoint). Do not rely on per-window MSE alone — it hides accumulated drift.

Sanity-check the physics first: implement a naive strapdown double-integrator and confirm it drifts unboundedly within seconds (a ~1 deg attitude error -> ~0.17 m/s^2 spurious horizontal accel -> meters of error in ~10 s). This baseline motivates and validates the windowed-regression design.

Hold out users AND devices for the test split (the original trained on one user/phone and tested on new users and different iPhones). Cross-device, cross-user generalization is the hard part; validate on non-periodic motion (trolley/stroller) where step-counting PDR fails.

citations.note: Situates IONet/L-IONet among learned inertial odometry methods; useful for understanding the polar-vector vs velocity-vector (RoNIN) design space.

pitfalls: Regressing global (x,y) position directly is the anti-pattern: it is not shift/rotation invariant, generalizes poorly to unseen start poses and headings, and forces the net to model the entire integration chain. IONet's whole point is to regress a frame-relative polar displacement instead. (Note: the paper motivates this by deriving the observable polar target rather than by an explicit ablation against position regression.)

Delta-psi is a RELATIVE heading change within the window, not an absolute heading. Confusing the two breaks trajectory reconstruction. Absolute heading is only obtained by accumulating Delta-psi (psi_n = psi_{n-1}+Delta-psi) starting from an initial psi_0 you must supply/estimate.

Delta-l is a scalar MAGNITUDE (always >= 0); it carries no direction. All directional information lives in Delta-psi. Do not try to regress a signed 2D displacement vector in the global frame and call it the same thing.

The orientation-independence only holds because of the L2 norm + orthogonality of the rotation matrix. If you change the displacement target to something that retains the rotation matrix (e.g., body-frame vector without taking the norm), the unknown initial orientation re-enters and the target becomes unobservable from a single window.

Heading still drifts. IONet bounds POSITION drift far better than strapdown, but accumulated Delta-psi errors mean long-trajectory heading can still wander; the magnetometer and loop closure are not part of the core method, so absolute orientation has no global correction.

Don't propagate LSTM/CNN hidden state across windows expecting continuity — the method deliberately treats windows independently. Carrying state reintroduces the wind-up/drift you were trying to avoid.
Scale mismatch in the loss: Delta-l is in meters, Delta-psi in radians. Without the kappa weighting the optimizer over-fits one term; tune kappa so the two error terms are comparable.

Sampling-rate mismatch: the published numbers assume 100 Hz with a 200-sample/2s window. A 200 Hz stream needs either downsampling or a doubled window length and label/stride recomputation, or the receptive field of the L-IONet dilated convs will cover only ~1 s of motion.

Per-window MSE is a misleading metric: a model with low polar MSE can still accumulate large trajectory drift. Always evaluate reconstructed-trajectory position error (CDF / error-at-distance) against VIO/mocap.

Train/test leakage across users and devices: the original protocol trains on one user/phone and tests on different users and phones. Splitting windows randomly across the same sequences inflates accuracy and hides the real cross-device generalization gap.

research.topic: Neural-network inertial navigation / pedestrian inertial odometry from smartphone IMU: TLIO (displacement+covariance ResNet + stochastic-cloning EKF), CTIN transformer, IMUNet, RNIN-VIO, with RoNIN as the foundational baseline. Detailed method specs (frame, output target, loss, architecture, uncertainty, EKF fusion).
key_techniques: GRAVITY-ALIGNED LOCAL FRAME (yaw-resolved): All four methods reject the raw body frame and reject the full world frame. They rotate the IMU window into a frame whose z-axis points along gravity but whose yaw (heading about gravity) is deliberately NOT globally resolved. TLIO builds the frame from the orientation at the START of each window (using filter+gyro rotation at runtime, VI-ground-truth rotation at training); RoNIN/CTIN call it the 'heading-agnostic' navigation frame. This makes the displacement/velocity target invariant to absolute heading, which is critical because heading-about-gravity is theoretically UNOBSERVABLE from IMU alone — putting data in this frame both injects the gravity-direction prior to the net and prevents the EKF update from injecting spurious yaw information.

TLIO INPUT/OUTPUT: input is N x 6 = 200 x 6 (200 samples of 3-axis accel + 3-axis gyro at 200 Hz = 1 s window), rotated into the gravity-aligned frame anchored at the window start. Output is two 3D vectors from independent fully-connected heads on top of a shared 1D-ResNet18 trunk: displacement d_hat (3D, the relative position change over the window expressed in the gravity-aligned frame) and uncertainty u_hat (3D log-std). Note TLIO regresses DISPLACEMENT directly (not velocity), so initial velocity is intentionally withheld from the net — the net learns only a 'typical human motion' prior, leaving velocity propagation to the EKF.

TLIO COVARIANCE PARAMETERIZATION: diagonal 3x3 only, parameterized by 3 coefficients via Sigma_hat = diag(exp(2*u_x), exp(2*u_y), exp(2*u_z)). Regressing log-std (not std or variance) removes the singularity at zero and stabilizes the NLL optimization. The diagonal assumption decouples axes and pins the uncertainty-ellipse principal axes to the gravity-aligned frame axes.

TLIO TWO-STAGE LOSS: (1) pretrain with plain MSE on displacement for ~10 epochs to stabilize the regression; (2) switch to Gaussian maximum-likelihood / negative-log-likelihood loss L_ML = mean over samples of [0.5*log det(Sigma_hat_i) + 0.5*||d_i - d_hat_i||^2_{Sigma_hat_i^-1}] + const, which jointly trains displacement and covariance. Training L_ML from scratch does NOT converge — the MSE warm-start is required. Adam, lr 1e-4, zero weight decay, dropout 0.5 on FC layers, ~10 more epochs, ~4 h on a DGX.

TLIO STOCHASTIC-CLONING EKF: a 15-dim current state s = (R, v, p, b_g, b_a) (rotation, velocity, position in world; gyro & accel biases) plus a sliding window of m cloned past poses xi_i = (R_i, p_i); full error-state dimension 6m+15. The filter propagates at IMU rate (200 Hz) with the strapdown kinematic model; at each update (20 Hz) it clones the current pose. The net's displacement is a RELATIVE measurement between cloned pose i and current pose j — stochastic cloning (Roumeliotis & Burdick 2002) is exactly the machinery for fusing such relative-state measurements.

TLIO MEASUREMENT MODEL (the key trick): the measurement function is NOT displacement in the world frame (that would make heading observable and inject false info). Instead h(X) = R_gamma^T (p_j - p_i), the displacement expressed in the LOCAL gravity-aligned frame anchored at clone i, where R_gamma is the YAW-ONLY rotation extracted from R_i via extrinsic XYZ Euler decomposition R_i = R_gamma R_beta R_alpha. The innovation is h(X) - d_hat_ij with covariance Sigma_hat_ij from the net. Kalman gain K = P H^T (H P H^T + Sigma_hat)^-1, Joseph-form covariance update. A chi-square gate (threshold 11.345 = 99th pct of chi2 with 3 dof) rejects bad net outputs.

TLIO TEMPORAL-CORRELATION HANDLING: because overlapping windows produce correlated measurements (violating the EKF white-noise assumption), TLIO inflates the network covariance by a factor of 10 at update time. The same IMU data is used twice (propagation input AND net measurement), violating independence; they mitigate this at training time by augmenting inputs with random bias perturbations (accel U[-0.2,0.2] m/s^2, gyro U[-0.05,0.05] rad/s) and random gravity-direction tilt (U[0,5 deg]) plus random horizontal-yaw rotation for yaw invariance.

CTIN TRANSFORMER ARCHITECTURE: a sequence-to-sequence encoder-decoder. SPATIAL ENCODER = ResNet-18 bottleneck blocks modified so the 3x3 spatial conv is replaced by a LOCAL self-attention layer (3x3 grid: 3x3 group conv produces local context C1 = X W_{K,3x3}, attention matrix gamma(Q,C1) via a concat/ReLU-projection form, attended map C2 = gamma(Q,C1)*V, output fuses local C1 + global C2), and a GLOBAL self-attention module (1x1 convs make Q,K,V; dot-product gamma) inserted before the last 1x1 downsampling conv. Number of layers / downsampling preserved from ResNet-18. TEMPORAL DECODER = N vanilla-Transformer decoder layers: masked (causal) self-attention over the temporal axis, then multi-head cross-attention over the encoder output to fuse spatial+temporal, then FFN; residual + LayerNorm around each sublayer. Embeddings: a 1D-CNN+BN+linear Spatial Embedding and a 1-layer BiLSTM Temporal Embedding plus a learned positional encoding.

CTIN OUTPUT & UNCERTAINTY: unlike TLIO, CTIN regresses 2D VELOCITY (vel_{1:m}) per timestep (RoNIN-style), with position obtained by integrating velocity, NOT displacement directly. Two MLP heads: a velocity head and a covariance head producing Sigma: x -> R^{2x2}, parameterized as a diagonal 2x2 (2 coefficients per velocity). Heading-agnostic navigation frame (z along gravity).

CTIN MULTI-TASK UNCERTAINTY LOSS: derived from Kendall-Gal homoscedastic uncertainty weighting. L = (1/(2*delta_v^2)) L_v + (1/(2*delta_c^2)) L_c + log(delta_v * delta_c), with learnable task-noise scalars delta_v, delta_c. L_v = Integral Velocity Loss (IVL) = L_pv + L_ev where L_pv is the L2 between positions integrated from predicted velocity and the ground-truth positional difference over the segment, and L_ev is the cumulative velocity error — i.e. supervise the INTEGRATED trajectory, not just per-step velocity. L_c = Covariance NLL (CNL) = 0.5*||y_v - f(x)||^2_{Sigma^-1} + 0.5*ln|Sigma|.

IMUNet (lightweight CNN for edge): keeps the 1D-ResNet18 macro-structure of RoNIN but replaces each standard 1D conv with a depthwise-separable conv (depthwise per-channel filter + pointwise 1x1 merge) inside a residual 'MobileResNet block' (MRBlock) with BatchNorm and ELU activation (not ReLU). Concrete table: input 6x200; Conv1D->64ch; 4 stages of MRBlock (2 layers each) at 64/128/256/512 channels; Conv1D->128ch; Dense->m (output dim). Depthwise conv per IMU axis also reduces cross-channel noise leakage. Output target = position/velocity regression like RoNIN (no covariance head). It is a drop-in efficiency-focused backbone, NOT an EKF system.

RNIN-VIO architecture (closest descendant of TLIO): RNIN = 1D-ResNet18 feature extractor -> standard LSTM that fuses temporal state across windows for continuous motion modeling -> 2 FC heads outputting 3D relative displacement + its covariance. The LSTM gives it memory across windows that TLIO's stateless ResNet lacks. Yaw-equivariant (gravity-aligned) frame, 200 Hz. Dual loss: a relative loss (local accuracy of each window) + an absolute loss (long-term global trajectory accuracy). Fused as a measurement update inside a tightly-coupled EKF that also ingests sparse visual features — and degrades gracefully to IMU-only when vision fails.

RoNIN baseline (the shared ancestor): input 200x6 at frame i (frames i-200..i, =1 s at 200 Hz), output 2D velocity in the heading-agnostic frame; three backbones (ResNet-18 1D, LSTM, TCN). For LSTM/TCN a 'latent velocity loss' integrates the regressed per-step vectors over 400/253 frames before computing loss, improving robustness to noisy targets. Position = cumulative integration of velocity. No covariance, no EKF — pure dead-reckoning by concatenation. TLIO's '3D-RONIN' baseline extends this to 3D + an AHRS heading filter.
concrete_recommendations: Adopt TLIO's exact split of responsibility for a clean rebuild: a STATELESS net that regresses only the relative displacement prior + uncertainty over a fixed window, and let a classical EKF own velocity, bias, and gravity propagation. Do NOT feed initial velocity to the net — withholding it forces the net to learn a pure motion prior and keeps the system modular and debuggable.

Use a gravity-aligned, yaw-UNRESOLVED local frame for BOTH net input and the measurement model. Build it from the orientation at the window start (filter+gyro at runtime; ground-truth VIO rotation at train time). Extract yaw-only R_gamma via extrinsic-XYZ Euler decomposition for the measurement function h = R_gamma^T (p_j - p_i). This single choice is what makes the system heading-observability-safe; getting the frame wrong is the most common reimplementation bug.

Parameterize the covariance as a DIAGONAL with log-std outputs: Sigma = diag(exp(2u_x), exp(2u_y), exp(2u_z)). Output log-std, never std/variance — it removes the zero-singularity and is what makes the NLL converge. Start with diagonal; only consider full/Cholesky parameterizations after diagonal is consistent.

Train in two stages: MSE warm-start (~10 epochs) then switch to Gaussian NLL. Joint NLL from scratch will not converge. Validate covariance CALIBRATION explicitly: plot predicted sigma vs realized error per axis and check that >~99% of errors fall within the 3-sigma cone, and that Mahalanobis distances pass a chi2 test. An uncalibrated covariance silently destroys the EKF — this check is non-optional.

Build the EKF as a stochastic-cloning filter: 15-dim current state (R, v, p, b_g, b_a) + sliding window of cloned poses (error-state dim 6m+15). Propagate at full IMU rate; clone + update at ~20 Hz. Marginalize poses older than the update window. Higher update frequency improved accuracy in TLIO despite increased temporal correlation.

Account for measurement correlation: inflate the net covariance (TLIO uses x10) because overlapping windows and double-use of IMU data violate EKF independence. Add a chi2 innovation gate (threshold ~11.345 for 3 dof at the 99th percentile) to reject occasional bad net outputs — this is a major robustness contributor in the ablations.

Augment training to harden against filter-fed input errors: random accel-bias U[-0.2,0.2] m/s^2, gyro-bias U[-0.05,0.05] rad/s, gravity-tilt U[0,5 deg], and random horizontal yaw for yaw invariance. TLIO's ablation shows these are what keep the net robust to the imperfect orientation/bias the filter feeds it at runtime, especially during initialization.

Decide displacement-target (TLIO/RNIN-VIO) vs velocity-target (RoNIN/CTIN) deliberately. Displacement + tight EKF gives lower drift and proper 3D/orientation estimation; velocity-regression + integration is simpler and more outlier-robust per-sample but needs an external heading filter. For a smartphone 200 Hz odometry rebuild aiming at low drift, the displacement+covariance+EKF (TLIO) path is the stronger reference.

If adding a transformer (CTIN-style), use a hybrid: a ResNet/CNN spatial encoder (optionally with local+global attention) feeding a small Transformer decoder for temporal fusion, and train with a multi-task uncertainty-weighted loss (Kendall-Gal) combining an INTEGRATED-trajectory loss (supervise integrated position, not just per-step velocity) with a covariance NLL. Note CTIN is heavier and was only evaluated as a dead-reckoning regressor, not inside an EKF.

For on-device/edge deployment, swap the ResNet-18 trunk for IMUNet-style depthwise-separable MobileResNet blocks (input 6x200, stages 64/128/256/512, ELU). It preserves RoNIN-level accuracy at a fraction of params/FLOPs and per-axis depthwise conv reduces cross-channel noise leakage — a good default backbone for the regressor regardless of whether you fuse with an EKF.

Standardize evaluation on ATE (RMSE of position over the trajectory), RTE/T-RTE (relative error over a 1 s or 60 s window, with yaw-drift removed at window start), and final drift (DR/PDE = final-position-error / path-length), plus separate yaw metrics (AYE/RYE). Report on RoNIN, RIDI, OxIOD (and IDOL) with seen/unseen subject splits to match the literature.

pitfalls: WRONG MEASUREMENT FRAME: defining the EKF displacement measurement in the world frame instead of the yaw-only local gravity-aligned frame makes heading observable and injects spurious yaw information into a state that is theoretically yaw-unobservable from IMU alone. You MUST rotate by yaw-only R_gamma (extrinsic-XYZ Euler decomposition of R_i), not the full rotation. This is TLIO's single most subtle and most-often-missed detail.

NLL TRAINING DIVERGENCE: training the Gaussian negative-log-likelihood loss from random init does not converge. Skip the MSE warm-start (TLIO ~10 epochs) and the covariance head will collapse or explode. Always two-stage.

COVARIANCE PARAMETERIZATION SINGULARITY: regressing variance or std directly hits a singularity/instability at zero in the NLL. Regress LOG-std and exponentiate (Sigma=diag(exp(2u))). Forgetting this is a common convergence failure.

TEMPORAL CORRELATION IGNORED: overlapping windows and double-use of the same IMU stream (propagation input AND net measurement) violate the EKF white-noise/independence assumption. Without covariance inflation (TLIO x10) and the chi2 innovation gate, the filter becomes overconfident and inconsistent; ablations show this is what separates a working system from a diverging one.

FEEDING INITIAL VELOCITY TO THE NET: tempting because it would improve raw regression, but it collapses the clean separation of concerns and lets the net leak filter state — TLIO deliberately withholds it so the net learns only a motion prior. Mixing the two also makes the system far harder to debug.

UNCALIBRATED UNCERTAINTY: a net can have low MSE but miscalibrated covariance; the EKF then weights measurements wrongly and can lose track (TLIO observed a fixed-covariance variant losing track at initialization). Always validate the 3-sigma coverage and Mahalanobis/chi2 consistency of the predicted covariance, not just point accuracy.

MSE-LOWER != ATE-LOWER: TLIO found that feeding more past data lowers per-sample MSE but does NOT lower trajectory ATE, because longer overlapping inputs increase temporal correlation of errors. Do not tune window/input length on MSE alone — evaluate end-to-end ATE/drift.

CONFUSING DISPLACEMENT vs VELOCITY TARGETS: TLIO/RNIN-VIO regress relative DISPLACEMENT and fuse via EKF; RoNIN/CTIN regress per-step VELOCITY and integrate. They need different supervision (positional/integrated loss vs per-step) and different downstream plumbing — conflating them (e.g., feeding velocity targets into a displacement-EKF measurement model) produces silently wrong trajectories.

STALE / SMARTPHONE-ESTIMATED ORIENTATION: the gravity-aligned frame is built from an orientation estimate (Android AHRS at test time in RoNIN/CTIN). Errors in that orientation directly corrupt the rotated input. TLIO mitigates with gravity-tilt augmentation; a clean rebuild must train with realistic orientation/bias perturbations or it will be brittle on real device orientation.

ASSUMING TRANSFORMER > CNN FOR FREE: CTIN beats RoNIN but is heavier and was evaluated only as a dead-reckoning regressor, not inside an EKF; IMUNet shows a depthwise-separable CNN matches RoNIN accuracy at far lower cost. Architecture choice should be driven by the deployment (edge vs server) and by whether you fuse with an EKF, not by assuming attention is strictly better.

research.topic: Coordinate frames, gravity, and rotation-equivariance in neural pedestrian inertial navigation (200Hz smartphone IMU): why global-frame displacement regression fails to generalize, the gravity-aligned/heading-agnostic frame, yaw augmentation, and strapdown drift characteristics
key_techniques: STRAPDOWN MECHANIZATION (the classical baseline the NN replaces). Steps: (1) integrate gyro to maintain orientation C(t) (body->nav rotation); (2) rotate body-frame accel into nav frame: a_g(t)=C(t)a_b(t); (3) subtract gravity g_g; (4) integrate once for velocity v_g, again for position s_g. Equations (Woodman): a_g=C a_b; v_g(t)=v_g(0)+INT(a_g - g_g)dt; s_g(t)=s_g(0)+INT v_g dt. This is the physics the learned model implicitly inverts.

DRIFT CHARACTERISTICS — the core motivation. (a) A constant accelerometer bias eps double-integrates into position error s(t)=eps*t^2/2 (QUADRATIC). (b) A constant gyro bias gives orientation/tilt error theta(t)=eps*t (LINEAR in time). (c) A tilt error theta leaks gravity onto the horizontal axes with magnitude g*sin(theta) ~= g*theta — this residual horizontal 'acceleration' double-integrates into position error ~ (1/2)*g*theta*t^2. Because theta itself grows linearly from gyro bias, gravity-leakage position error grows as t^3 (CUBIC) — the dominant error path. Woodman's concrete number: a 0.05deg tilt leaks 0.0086 m/s^2 and produces 7.7 m of horizontal position error in 30 s; a stationary Xsens MTx drifted 152.67 m in 60 s, with only 1.76 m of that in z — i.e. essentially all drift is horizontal gravity-leakage from orientation error.

WHY DIRECT GLOBAL-FRAME REGRESSION FROM RAW BODY-FRAME IMU FAILS TO GENERALIZE. Raw IMU is in the body/device frame, which depends on arbitrary device attachment (yaw/roll/pitch) and on the user's global heading. If you map raw body-frame IMU -> global displacement, the same physical motion produces different (input, target) pairs under every device orientation and every walking heading. The acc/gyro signature of 'walk forward' is identical regardless of compass heading, but the global-frame target rotates with heading. The network must memorize all heading/orientation combinations — it cannot, so it overfits to the headings/placements seen in training and degrades on unseen ones. (IONet: 'orientation transformations impact all subsequent outputs'; EqNIO: networks 'must learn to ignore data variations due to specific IMU mount orientation and motion directions, hindering generalization', and show large trajectory error 'when observing simply rotated input data' even with augmentation.)

GRAVITY REMOVAL / OBSERVABILITY. Gravity g dominates the accelerometer (g >> typical pedestrian acceleration), so it must be removed before integration; doing so requires knowing orientation relative to gravity. Roll and pitch (tilt) ARE observable from the gravity vector when quasi-static, so the gravity direction can be recovered from accel or an off-the-shelf orientation filter/EKF. YAW (heading about gravity) is NOT observable from accel+gyro alone (no absolute heading reference without a magnetometer) — this unobservability is exactly why methods make the regression target yaw-invariant rather than predicting global heading.

HEADING-AGNOSTIC / GRAVITY-ALIGNED COORDINATE FRAME (HACF, RoNIN). Define a frame whose Z-axis is aligned with gravity but whose horizontal (yaw) orientation is arbitrary. Rotate the IMU window into this frame using device orientation (Android Game Rotation Vector / iOS / EKF) and regress the motion target in this frame. Because Z is pinned to gravity, tilt/placement variation is removed; because the horizontal axes are deliberately treated as arbitrary (and randomized in training), the network learns a heading-invariant input->output map. RoNIN regresses a 2D velocity vector in the HACF over a 200-frame (200Hz) window.

TLIO GRAVITY-ALIGNED LOCAL FRAME + DISPLACEMENT-WITH-COVARIANCE. Rotate each IMU window from the IMU frame to a gravity-aligned frame built from the orientation at the START of the window, then regress a 3D displacement d-hat AND a diagonal covariance Sigma-hat over a 1s window (200 samples). Using a local gravity-aligned frame keeps unobservable global yaw out of the measurement (the EKF measurement h(X)=R_gamma^T (p_j - p_i) only depends on relative motion). Covariance parametrized as Sigma=diag(e^{2u_x},e^{2u_y},e^{2u_z}); fused into a stochastic-cloning EKF for pose/velocity/bias.

ROTATION-EQUIVARIANCE AS THE PRINCIPLED FIX (EqNIO). Yaw augmentation only approximates invariance; an O(2)-equivariant network guarantees it. The relevant symmetry is roto-reflections that preserve gravity (O_g(3) ~= O(2)): rotations about the gravity/Z axis plus reflections across vertical planes. Under such a transform R: accel transforms a'=R a (equivariant), angular velocity w'=det(R) R w (a PSEUDOVECTOR — flips sign under reflection), displacement d'=R d (equivariant), covariance vec(Sigma') = (R⊗R) vec(Sigma). EqNIO canonicalizes in two steps: (1) gravity-align Z from the EKF, (2) predict a LEARNED canonical yaw frame F (its 3 axes: Z=gravity fixed, the other two predicted equivariantly from IMU); regress displacement/cov in the canonical frame and map back with d=F d'. Improves on RoNIN/TLIO baselines and converges far faster (~38 vs >100 epochs).

IONet POLAR (HEADING-RELATIVE) FORMULATION. Segment the continuous integration into independent windows (200 frames @100Hz = 2s) to break unbounded error accumulation. Instead of a global displacement, regress a POLAR delta vector (delta-L, delta-psi): the horizontal distance traveled and the CHANGE in heading over the window — both relative quantities that depend only on the IMU sequence (plus latent initial velocity & body-frame gravity), not on absolute heading. f_theta: (a,w)_{200x6} -> (delta-l, delta-psi)_{1x2} via a 2-layer bidirectional LSTM. Polar/relative targets are inherently heading-invariant without needing an external orientation frame.

YAW / RANDOM-ROTATION-ABOUT-GRAVITY DATA AUGMENTATION. At each training step apply a random rotation about the gravity (Z) axis to BOTH the gravity-aligned IMU input and the ground-truth target (e.g. rotate the 2D velocity / 3D displacement by the same yaw). This teaches the network that heading is irrelevant and forces a heading-invariant map; it is the cheap, architecture-agnostic substitute for true O(2) equivariance. RoNIN uses a random HACF per step; TLIO applies random horizontal rotation per sample plus small (0-5deg) random gravity-direction perturbation and accel/gyro bias perturbations for robustness.

EVALUATION METRICS. ATE (Absolute Trajectory Error): RMSE between estimated and ground-truth positions over the whole trajectory (after alignment). RTE (Relative Trajectory Error): RMSE over a fixed time interval (RoNIN uses 1 minute). TLIO/EqNIO additionally report MSE of the windowed displacement and yaw/position drift rates. Report ATE and RTE in meters.
concrete_recommendations: Do NOT regress global-frame position or displacement from raw body-frame IMU. Pick a heading-invariant target. Recommended default for a clean reimplementation: RoNIN-style regress a 2D horizontal velocity vector in a gravity-aligned, heading-agnostic frame over a sliding window (the proven, simplest strong baseline).

Build the gravity-aligned frame explicitly. At inference, get device orientation from the platform (Android Game Rotation Vector / iOS CMAttitude / Madgwick or Mahony AHRS) and rotate the accel+gyro window so Z is along gravity. Do NOT rely on the network to discover gravity. Tilt (roll/pitch) is observable; pin it. Leave horizontal yaw arbitrary.

Make the target 2D and horizontal. Pedestrian vertical motion averages ~0 over a window; predicting 2D horizontal velocity/displacement removes the noisy/unobservable vertical component (IONet explicitly assumes zero mean z-displacement over a window).

ALWAYS apply random-yaw (rotation-about-gravity) augmentation. Each batch/step, draw a random angle, rotate the gravity-aligned IMU input AND the target velocity/displacement by that same angle. This is the single highest-leverage trick for generalization and is mandatory if you are NOT using an equivariant architecture. Also add small gravity-direction jitter (~0-5deg) and accel/gyro bias jitter (TLIO ranges: acc [-0.2,0.2] m/s^2, gyro [-0.05,0.05] rad/s) for orientation-error robustness.

Use a 1D ResNet-18 (channels-as-features, time-as-length) over a ~1-2 s window at 200Hz as the backbone — it is the common, strong choice in RoNIN and TLIO and trains faster/more stably than the LSTM/TCN variants. Input tensor 200x6 (acc xyz + gyro xyz). Loss: MSE on the velocity/displacement target; warm up with MSE then switch to Gaussian NLL if you also regress covariance.

If you can afford an orientation filter + light fusion, adopt the TLIO structure: regress 3D displacement + diagonal covariance (Sigma=diag(e^{2u})) per 1 s window in a frame gravity-aligned to the window START, train MSE for ~10 epochs then Gaussian MLE, and fuse into a stochastic-cloning EKF that estimates pose/velocity/biases. This bounds drift far better than open-loop velocity integration (~27% yaw / 33% position improvement over RoNIN concat in TLIO).

For maximum robustness to unseen orientations, consider an O(2)-equivariant design (EqNIO): canonicalize by gravity-align then learned canonical-yaw frame, regress in the canonical frame, map back. Treat angular velocity as a PSEUDOVECTOR (w' = det(R) R w) — getting the reflection sign wrong silently breaks equivariance. This guarantees what augmentation only approximates and converges faster.

Magnetometer: do NOT feed raw magnetometer into the position regressor and do NOT use it to define the regression frame (indoor magnetic disturbance is severe and would re-introduce heading variance). Use it, if at all, only as a slow absolute-yaw correction in a separate orientation filter / global heading estimate, kept out of the displacement network. The displacement network should remain yaw-invariant.

Resample/clean to a fixed 200Hz with consistent dt before windowing; integration update v(t+dt)=v(t)+dt*(a_g(t+dt)-g_g) assumes uniform sampling. Subtract a calibrated/estimated accel bias and the gravity vector in the gravity-aligned frame before any integration in your strapdown reference baseline.

Implement a strapdown-mechanization baseline to quantify the problem: it will exhibit the cubic (gyro-bias->gravity-leakage) position drift and tens-to-hundreds of meters of error per minute (Woodman: 152 m in 60 s stationary). Use it as the lower bound the learned model must beat, and as a sanity check that your frame/gravity handling is correct.

Evaluate with ATE (whole-trajectory RMSE after rigid/Umeyama alignment) and RTE over a fixed 1-minute window, both in meters; report on held-out subjects AND held-out device orientations/headings to actually measure generalization (this is where global-frame regressors collapse).

pitfalls: Feeding raw body-frame IMU and regressing a GLOBAL-frame target. This couples the target to arbitrary device placement and walking heading; the network memorizes seen headings and fails on unseen ones. This is the #1 cause of poor generalization and the entire reason the gravity-aligned/heading-agnostic frame exists.

Skipping yaw augmentation when using a non-equivariant network. Without random-rotation-about-gravity augmentation, even a gravity-aligned model will overfit to the heading distribution of the training trajectories. Augmentation is effectively mandatory.

Rotating only the input or only the target during yaw augmentation. You MUST apply the SAME random yaw to both the gravity-aligned IMU window and the supervision target, or you destroy the input->output correspondence.

Treating angular velocity as an ordinary vector under reflection. Gyro readings are a pseudovector: under a reflection they pick up a det(R) sign flip (omega' = det(R) R omega). Equivariant implementations that miss this silently lose the guarantee; even augmentation-only pipelines should be aware when adding mirror augmentation.

Trusting the network to remove gravity / discover the vertical. Gravity (~9.8 m/s^2) swamps pedestrian acceleration; you must subtract it using an orientation estimate. Omitting explicit gravity alignment leaves a huge orientation-dependent bias that re-introduces tilt sensitivity.

Letting yaw into the regression target or the frame definition. Yaw about gravity is unobservable from accel+gyro; predicting absolute heading or building the frame from a (disturbed indoor) magnetometer reinjects the heading variance you were trying to remove. Keep the displacement target relative/heading-invariant.

Using the magnetometer naively for the displacement frame indoors. Indoor magnetic fields are heavily distorted by structures/electronics; magnetometer-defined headings are unreliable and will corrupt a heading-agnostic pipeline. Confine the magnetometer to a slow, separate absolute-heading correction outside the displacement network.

Underestimating drift order in the baseline: open-loop strapdown position error from orientation error is CUBIC in time (gyro bias -> linear tilt -> gravity leakage -> double integration), not merely quadratic. Expect tens to hundreds of meters per minute. If your learned model isn't dramatically better, your frame/gravity handling is likely wrong.

Non-uniform / mismatched sampling. Mechanization and windowing assume a fixed dt (commonly 200Hz). Jittered timestamps or mismatched IMU/ground-truth rates corrupt both the strapdown baseline and the learned velocity-integration target.

Evaluating only on held-out time/subjects but the SAME device orientations and headings as training. This hides the exact failure mode under study. Always include held-out orientation/heading splits to expose rotation-variance.

Omitting bias/gravity-direction perturbation augmentation. Real orientation estimates have residual tilt and the IMU has time-varying bias; training only on clean gravity-aligned data makes the model brittle to the small orientation errors that dominate real drift.

research.topic: Discrete-time quaternion attitude propagation from gyroscope, AHRS orientation filters (Madgwick, Mahony, EKF), and the Brossard 2020 deep-learning gyro denoising method — for a clean reference reimplementation of neural inertial navigation from smartphone IMU at ~200 Hz.
key_techniques: EXACT CLOSED-FORM PROPAGATION (verified, AHRS docs): for body-frame angular rate w=[wx,wy,wz] held constant over dt, q_{k+1} = [cos(|w|dt/2) I_4 + (1/|w|) sin(|w|dt/2) Omega(w)] q_k. This is exact (the quaternion exponential / Euler-Rodrigues map), automatically preserves unit norm in exact arithmetic, and reduces to identity when |w|->0. Renormalize each step to fight float drift.

OMEGA(w) 4x4 MATRIX, scalar-first convention q=[qw,qx,qy,qz]: Omega(w) = [[0,-wx,-wy,-wz],[wx,0,wz,-wy],[wy,-wz,0,wx],[wz,wy,-wx,0]]. It is skew-symmetric (Omega^T = -Omega). Note this equals 2x the matrix that implements the Hamilton product (1/2) q (x) [0,w]; i.e. q_dot = (1/2) Omega(w) q. The closed form is the matrix exponential exp((dt/2)Omega(w)).

CONVENTION DISCIPLINE (the #1 reimplementation footgun): scalar-FIRST [w,x,y,z] (Eigen, ahrs library, Madgwick report, Brossard) vs scalar-LAST [x,y,z,w] (SciPy Rotation, ROS/tf, JPL-style). The exact form of Omega(w), the order of Hamilton products, and library round-trips ALL change with convention. Also distinguish Hamilton (q1 q2 right-to-left, ij=k) vs JPL convention. Pick scalar-first Hamilton and assert it everywhere with unit tests.

ZEROTH-ORDER (forward-Euler / first-order series) INTEGRATION VARIANT: q_{k+1} = [I_4 + (dt/2) Omega(w)] q_k, then renormalize. This is the first-order Taylor truncation of the matrix exponential; cheap, common on embedded targets, but does NOT preserve norm and accumulates error for large |w|*dt. Higher-order series add accuracy but can diverge on unfiltered noisy signals.

MIDPOINT / FIRST-ORDER (better) VARIANT: use averaged angular rate w_avg = (w_k + w_{k+1})/2 inside the closed-form, or the closed-form itself which is the gold standard. The closed-form (full exponential) is preferred over Euler when |w|*dt is non-negligible; at 200 Hz (dt=5 ms) with moderate rates the difference is small but matters over long open-loop dead reckoning.

MADGWICK FILTER (gradient-descent AHRS, original report Madgwick 2010, IMU+MARG): gyro term q_dot_w = (1/2) q (x) [0,w]; correction minimizes objective f(q, E_d, S_s) = q* (x) E_d (x) q - S_s aligning Earth-frame reference E_d (gravity E_g=[0,0,0,1]; magnetic E_b=[0,bx,0,bz]) to normalized sensor measurement; gradient grad f = J^T f; fused rate q_dot = q_dot_w - beta * (grad f)/||grad f||; integrate q_{k+1} = q_k + q_dot*dt then renormalize. Gain beta = sqrt(3/4) * w_bar where w_bar is mean gyro error (rad/s). IMU variant (acc+gyro) fixes only roll/pitch; MARG variant (acc+gyro+mag) adds heading via a magnetic distortion compensation step E_h = q (x) [0,m] (x) q* projected to [bx,0,bz].

MAHONY FILTER (explicit/passive nonlinear complementary observer on SO(3), Mahony et al. 2008): error term w_mes = sum_i k_i (v_i x v_hat_i) cross products of measured vs estimated reference directions (acc->gravity, mag->magnetic north); PI feedback: bias update b_dot = -k_I * w_mes; corrected rate fed to kinematics q_dot = (1/2) q (x) [0, (w_gyro - b_hat + k_P*w_mes)]; integrate and renormalize. Default gains k_P=1, k_I=0.3. The integral term estimates and removes slow gyro bias online — useful since smartphone MEMS gyros are biased.

EKF QUATERNION ORIENTATION FILTER: state typically 4 quaternion + 3 gyro-bias = 7 (error-state/MEKF variants use a 3-DoF rotation error to keep covariance non-singular). PREDICT: propagate q with the closed-form/Euler gyro integration; gyro noise + bias random walk enters as PROCESS noise (gyro is an input, not a measurement). UPDATE: accelerometer (and magnetometer) treated as MEASUREMENTS of the gravity (and magnetic) direction in body frame; innovation corrects roll/pitch (and yaw). Multiplicative EKF (MEKF) is the robust standard; quaternion normalization handled via the error-state injection.

BROSSARD 2020 'Denoising IMU Gyroscopes with Deep Learning' CORE IDEA: a dilated CNN regresses a small gyro CORRECTION; corrected noise-free rate w_hat_n = C_hat_w * w_imu_n + ĉ_n where C_hat_w in R^{3x3} are STATIC learned intrinsic (axis-misalignment+scale) params initialized to I_3, and ĉ_n is the time-varying network output that ABSORBS the gyro bias (ĉ_n = e_n + b). Attitude is then pure OPEN-LOOP integration of w_hat via R_n = R_{n-1} exp(w_hat_n dt). No accelerometer-based correction at inference (open loop); accelerometers ARE fed as network input (ablation: removing them => +50% ROE).

BROSSARD ARCHITECTURE (Fig.2, verified vs paper + repo): 5-layer 1D dilated CNN over the past window. kernel dims [7,7,7,7,1]; dilation gaps [1,4,16,64,1]; channel dims [16,32,64,128,1]; between conv layers: batchnorm + GELU activation (GELU/ELU smooth activations beat ReLU which overfits sharp corrections). Receptive field N = max(kernel*dilation) = 7*64 = 448 samples = 2.24 s of past IMU at 200 Hz. Only ~77,052 params (vs >2.6M for VIO learning baselines). Input = 6-DoF IMU (gyro + accel). No RNN (LSTM variant gave ~40% more ROE).

BROSSARD LOSS (the load-bearing trick): never needs ground-truth rate at 200 Hz (mocap is only 20-120 Hz). Define integrated increments dR_{i,i+j} = R_i^T R_{i+j} = prod_{k=i}^{i+j-1} exp(w_k dt). Per-scale loss L_j = sum_i rho( log( dR_{i,i+j} dR_hat_{i,i+j}^T ) ) where log() is the SO(3) log map and rho is the Huber loss (Huber param = 0.005). Total loss L = L_16 + L_32 (increments at 200/16≈12.5 Hz and 200/32≈6.25 Hz). Huber gives robustness to ground-truth outliers; integrating over windows (16/32) is rotation-invariant and avoids overfitting to per-sample noise; too-large j overfits trajectory patterns.

BROSSARD TRAINING SETUP (verified): PyTorch 1.5; ADAM optimizer; LR initialized 0.01 with COSINE warm-restart schedule; 1800 epochs (~<5 min/dataset on a GTX 1080); weight decay 0.1 and dropout 0.1 (both needed against overfitting, ~77k params vs ~90k EuRoC / ~45k TUM-VI training points); data augmentation = add Gaussian gyro noise (std = half the dataset's, 0.01 deg/s). Train only on the FIRST 50 s (best mocap accuracy) — 8 minutes of data suffices.

BROSSARD EVALUATION METRICS (use these for benchmarking): Absolute Orientation Error AOE = sqrt( (1/M) sum_n || log(R_n^T R_hat_n) ||_2^2 ) in degrees, after aligning at n=0 (AOE is sensitive to where error occurs). Relative Orientation Error ROE = || log( dR_{n,g(n)}^T dR_hat_{n,g(n)} ) ||_2 collected over sub-trajectories of fixed travelled distance (7/21/35 m), reported as median/percentiles — the RECOMMENDED odometry metric. Report both 3D-orientation and yaw-only. Results: median ~1.34 deg/min (EuRoC), ~0.68 deg/min (TUM-VI), beating OriNet and competing with VIO without vision.
concrete_recommendations: Implement ONE quaternion module with an explicit, asserted convention: scalar-first Hamilton q=[w,x,y,z]. Provide quat_mul (Hamilton), quat_conj, quat_norm, quat_to_rotmat, rotmat_to_quat, and quat_exp/quat_log. Write round-trip unit tests against SciPy (which is scalar-LAST x,y,z,w) with an explicit index permutation in the test, so the convention mismatch is caught, not silently absorbed.

Make the gyro propagator the exact closed-form q_{k+1} = [cos(|w|dt/2) I + sin(|w|dt/2)/|w| Omega(w)] q_k with the documented Omega(w) = [[0,-wx,-wy,-wz],[wx,0,wz,-wy],[wy,-wz,0,wx],[wz,wy,-wx,0]]. Add a |w|->0 guard (Taylor: cos~1, sin/|w|~dt/2) to avoid division by zero, and renormalize every step. Keep the first-order variant q_{k+1}=(I + (dt/2)Omega(w))q_k behind a flag for speed/ablation only.

Prefer rotation-MATRIX or SO(3) representation internally for the training loss (so you can use the SO(3) log map cleanly), but you can store/propagate as quaternion — the Brossard paper explicitly states quaternion and rotation-matrix loss implementations give identical accuracy once unit norm is enforced. Use a batched, differentiable SO(3) exp/log (e.g. via the Rodrigues formula) so the loss backprops through the integration.

Reproduce Brossard exactly for the gyro-denoising front end: 5 dilated 1D-conv layers, kernels [7,7,7,7,1], dilations [1,4,16,64,1], channels [16,32,64,128,1], BatchNorm+GELU between layers, input = 6-axis IMU window of 448 samples (2.24 s at 200 Hz), output = 3-vector correction ĉ_n; add a static learned 3x3 C_w initialized to identity; corrected rate w_hat = C_w w_imu + ĉ. This is ~77k params — keep it tiny.

Use the multi-scale increment loss L = L_16 + L_32 with Huber(delta=0.005) on log(dR_true dR_hat^T), where dR over a window of j samples is the product of per-sample exp(w_hat dt). Do NOT define the loss on per-sample rate error (no 200 Hz ground truth exists) and do NOT use whole-trajectory orientation error (overfits). Precompute ground-truth dR_{i,i+j} once and reuse (tree-of-products for efficiency).

Train with ADAM, LR=0.01 + cosine warm restarts, weight decay 0.1, dropout 0.1, ~1800 epochs; augment with Gaussian gyro noise (std ~0.01 deg/s, half the dataset std). On smartphone data, ensure CONSTANT sampling time and tight time-alignment between IMU and ground truth — the paper flags time misalignment as causing the net to learn a spurious delay; resample to a fixed 200 Hz grid first.

Evaluate with BOTH AOE = sqrt((1/M) sum ||log(R_n^T R_hat_n)||^2) (aligned at t=0) and ROE = ||log(dR^T dR_hat)|| over fixed travelled-distance sub-windows (report median + percentiles). Report 3D and yaw-only separately. Compare against three baselines in-repo: raw IMU integration, calibrated-IMU (set net input to 0 so only C_w/bias act), and a classical AHRS (Madgwick/Mahony) — this isolates how much the neural correction actually buys.

Ship classical AHRS filters as both baselines and bias-bootstrap: implement Madgwick (gain beta from gyro noise, MARG variant for heading) and Mahony (k_P=1, k_I=0.3, with the integral term giving online bias estimation). For smartphone pedestrian use, the magnetometer is noisy/perturbed indoors — gate or down-weight the magnetic correction (or run IMU-only and accept yaw drift, which the Brossard open-loop integrator addresses for short windows).

For an EKF baseline, use a Multiplicative EKF (error-state, 3-DoF rotation error + 3 gyro-bias states) rather than a naive 4-quaternion EKF, to avoid the singular/over-parameterized covariance and the renormalization hacks; gyro drives PREDICT (its noise is process noise), accelerometer/magnetometer drive UPDATE as direction measurements.

Keep the frame definitions explicit in code and docstrings: w is the BODY-frame angular rate; R_n maps body->global (world/navigation, typically ENU or NED — pick one); accelerometer measures specific force a = R^T(v_dot - g) so gravity sign and frame must match. Mis-specified gravity sign or body/world direction is the second most common dead-reckoning bug after quaternion convention.
